name: Bitcoin For The Arts
about:
Bitcoin for the Arts, Inc. (BFTA) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit empowering sovereign creators in visual arts, theater, dance, music, writing, storytelling, and film—exclusively through Bitcoin. Fueling a cultural renaissance with sound money grants, workshops, artist stories, and our decentralized Nostr Artist Hub.

releases.title: Mr. Meadow: Bitcoin Deserves Better Visuals
releases.summary:
Mr. Meadow is a Bitcoin artist and filmmaker in India. He prices the work in sats. The site is mrmeadow.org.
He found Bitcoin in 2017 through a friend and bought some, then spent the next years on altcoins because he could not yet tell signal from noise. He designed for a friend's wallet company, spent time at Deloitte, and worked with a Polkadot India team that was training coders in Rust and chasing funding. releases.title: Benjamin Ella: Seventeen Seasons at the Royal Ballet, Then Bitcoin
releases.summary:
Benjamin Ella danced seventeen seasons as a soloist of the Royal Ballet. He arrived from Melbourne at fifteen on a full scholarship, graduated with a stress fracture in the navicular, and was kept by Dame Monica Mason while two titanium pins and three hard years decided whether he would dance at all.
In this episode of Share Your Bitcoin Journey, Bitcoin For The Arts founder Dion Wilson sits down with him. Two dancers, London and New York, who both ended up on the union side of the table. Benjamin talks about a family ballet school that refused government grants, a first bitcoin purchase in 20

releases.title: Bitbrand: Bitcoin Saved My Life
releases.summary:
Bitbrand makes hand-branded Bitcoin goods the old way: steel, fire, and leather. No ink, no printer, and no two pieces alike. He invented the Bitcoin branding iron, calls himself the branding iron broker, and built the company from the back of a van.
In this episode of Share Your Bitcoin Journey, Bitcoin For The Arts founder Dion Wilson meets Bitbrand in Jersey City, after they first met at the Midwest Bitcoin Summit in Columbus. Bitbrand tells how Bitcoin saved his life, how an ATM on the Upper East Side changed what he did with his money, and how he got sober at 30 and quit the corporate job

releases.title: Sara Jade: A Million Sats in One Set
releases.summary:
Sara Jade is a keytar player and cinematic pop-rock songwriter. She built a following of more than 30,000 on Nostr, gets zapped in real time on TuneStr, and lives on a Bitcoin standard.
In this episode of Share Your Bitcoin Journey, Bitcoin For The Arts founder Dion Wilson sits down with Sara about leaving the old streaming economy. She tells the story of earning a million sats in a single acoustic set, from people in the room and people watching online. She explains why Spotify removed one of her singles for phantom streaming, and what it meant to open for Jason Mraz while stacking sats inste

releases.title: Joe Martin: It's All About the Song
releases.summary:
Joe Martin is a singer-songwriter and a 21st century troubadour. The song comes first. He grew up in the UK, learned piano as a child, picked up his father's guitar as a teenager, and has spent a decade writing Americana and country, with trips to Nashville along the way. He is based on the Isle of Man. He is fully independent. He sells merch for sats.
In this episode, Bitcoin For The Arts founder Dion Wilson talks with Joe about Alone in Valentine, the album he made on purpose without AI. He recorded it in Nashville with Cal Campbell, son of Glen Campbell, and Cornelius Webb, son of Jimmy Web

releases.title: Fzero: The Artist Creates First
releases.summary: Fzero is a designer, illustrator, node runner, and co-founder of Ninefold, the studio he runs with Ivy Lumi. Their line is "stories that make you build." He started by copying manga as a kid. He studied economics, finance, and marketing, then opened stores and ran the floor for big fashion brands. The work looked like a career. It did not feel like one. On December 25, still under 30 and home with his family, he had a stroke. He already knew Bitcoin. He had been stacking sats for years. The scare settled the question. releases.title: Thomas Forsyth: The General Handychap Path to Sound Money
releases.summary:
Thomas Forsyth is a London designer, maker, and engineer. His work spans the Saatchi Gallery, Glastonbury Festival, the Wall Street Journal's Apple Car, and a Star Wars K-2SO build for Silicon Valley Comic Con. He calls himself a general handychap.
In this episode, Bitcoin For The Arts founder Dion Wilson talks with Thomas about why he uses that name, the three times Bitcoin showed up before it clicked, and why sound money and sound craft share a backbone.
Bitcoin crossed his path three times. First in a London bar around 2010. Then in 2018, while he was teaching himself about money. Then in 2

releases.title: The Higher Low: Songs About Bitcoin That Never Say Bitcoin
releases.summary:
Rami Korhonen has sung in the Finnish melodic punk band Fumble since the early nineties. One of their songs opens an episode of Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. A few years ago, on long business trips in the Middle East, he picked up a guitar he found in a rented apartment and started writing songs about Bitcoin, with one rule: the songs never say the word. He calls it acoustic pleb rock. The project is The Higher Low.
In this episode, Bitcoin For The Arts founder Dion Wilson sits down with Rami to trace the whole road: seeing the Ramones in Helsinki at sixteen, thirty years of DIY punk, rec

releases.title: Depicting Bitcoin: Anik Malcolm and The Whole Entire Universe
releases.summary:
Classically trained in London, disillusioned in Reykjavik, now in the mountains of central Italy with his family, Anik Malcolm makes some of the most rigorous fine art in the Bitcoin space. Tagline: Depicting Bitcoin. Main work: The Whole Entire Universe, debuted at Bitcoin 2026 in Las Vegas after 900+ hours. Twenty-one million beads. Cube of 276 by 276 by 276. Each face 4,096 squares. The halving pattern lives in the image, and it only works cleanly at 21 million.

Dion talks with Anik from childhood making, to London training, to the gallery moment that broke the spell, to Italy, to Bitcoin

releases.title: Philip Charter: The Totally Human Writer
releases.summary:
In this conversation, Bitcoin For The Arts founder Dion Wilson sits down with Philip Charter, the British author, editor, and ghostwriter behind Totally Human Writer, and the co-editor of 21 Futures, the world's first Bitcoin fiction anthology.
Philip lives in Gran Canaria. He is the co-editor of 21 Futures: Tales from the Timechain, a collection of twenty-one stories from twenty-one authors including Knut Svanholm and Ioni Appelberg, released by Konsensus Network in 2023 and presented at Bitcoin Atlantis in 2024. releases.title: Alana Mediavilla: The Filmmaker Behind Dirty Coin
releases.summary:
In this conversation, Bitcoin For The Arts founder Dion Wilson sits down with Alana Mediavilla, the Puerto Rican filmmaker behind the award-winning documentary Dirty Coin and founder of Campo Libre in San Juan.
Alana spent more than a decade inside Silicon Valley producing for Google, Apple, PayPal, Volkswagen, and Volvo, including four years as a video producer for Google Cloud. In 2020 she walked away, moved her family home to Puerto Rico, and built the most important documentary on Bitcoin mining ever made. releases.title: From Widow to Bitcoin Author: A Mother's Journey with Lindey Magee  Description
releases.summary:
Mississippi mother Lindey Magee never planned to become a Bitcoin author. In August 2024, her husband Chuck lost his battle with cancer after twenty-five years of marriage, leaving her a widow with two children and no traditional income. Twelve years earlier, her then-twelve-year-old son Bennett had tried to teach her about Bitcoin. In grief, that conversation came back.

In this episode of Share Your Bitcoin Journey, Bitcoin For The Arts founder Dion Wilson sits down with Lindey Magee, author of the Seuss-style rhyming children's book Bitcoin: A Treasure to HODL, which debuted at Bitcoin 2025

releases.title: James Kintore: Materials-First Path from Sydney to Sound Money
releases.summary:
Australian interior designer James Kintore — founder of Kintore Design and co-creator of Mat and Kin — on materiality, the time chain, and designing for things that last.
From rural South Australia to high-end Sydney residential work, then a 2025 move to Costa Rica to rebuild on a Bitcoin standard. We talk the 250-year-old French oak, the 2020 money-printer awakening, why Bitcoin is "an energy agreement," HNW clients and the Australian dollar, and why AI raises the value of real human creation.

releases.title: Lady Nakamoto: From the X Games to Bitcoin Art
releases.summary:
Alaskan digital artist Lady Nakamoto sits down for her first full interview. Former X Games and World Cup snowboarder. Rolf Institute graduate. Creator of Along the Watchtower, The Patriot, and The Greatest War.
We go from Girdwood and the Alyeska ski mountain to Bitcoin in 2010, years in the wilderness, a vision quest, and the birth of Lady Nakamoto. She represented Bitcoin for the Arts at Bitcoin Is For Everyone in Portland and sold her first artwork peer-to-peer with Bitcoin.
A conversation about sovereignty, wholeness, and why peer-to-peer is the most overlooked line in the white paper.
